message.content:
Read-only survey of the Fortress codebase at /home/user/fortress to size an ASM 3.1 → ASM 9.x migration. Do NOT modify any files. Search breadth: very thorough.

Context: ~58 Java files import org.objectweb.asm (vendored jar is ProjectFortress/third_party/asm/asm-all-3.1.jar). The key ASM 3→4+ breaking changes are:
1. ClassVisitor/MethodVisitor/FieldVisitor/AnnotationVisitor changed from interfaces to abstract classes with an `api` constructor argument; ClassAdapter and MethodAdapter were removed (replaced by extending ClassVisitor/MethodVisitor directly).
2. visitMethodInsn gained a 5-arg form with a trailing boolean `itf` (the 4-arg form is deprecated/removed depending on version).
3. ClassWriter flags / COMPUTE_FRAMES semantics, ClassReader.accept flags.
4. org.objectweb.asm.util (TraceClassVisitor, CheckClassAdapter), org.objectweb.asm.commons, org.objectweb.asm.tree sub-packages — in ASM 9 these live in separate artifacts (asm-util, asm-commons, asm-tree) rather than one asm-all jar.

Survey all files under ProjectFortress/src that import org.objectweb.asm and report:

A. Every class that `implements ClassVisitor`, `implements MethodVisitor`, `implements FieldVisitor`, `implements AnnotationVisitor`, or any other ASM visitor interface — list file, class name, which interface(s). These need conversion to `extends` with api arg.
B. Every class that `extends ClassAdapter` or `extends MethodAdapter` or extends ClassWriter/ClassVisitor/MethodVisitor/other ASM classes — list file, class, superclass.
C. Which sub-packages are used: count/list imports of org.objectweb.asm.util.*, org.objectweb.asm.commons.*, org.objectweb.asm.tree.*, and any others beyond the core package.
D. visitMethodInsn usage: how many call sites (rough count per file), and whether any file *overrides* visitMethodInsn (those signatures must change).
E. ClassWriter instantiations: list each `new ClassWriter(...)` with the flags used (COMPUTE_MAXS/COMPUTE_FRAMES/0), and each ClassReader usage (what accept flags).
F. Any use of ASM internals that changed: e.g. `org.objectweb.asm.Attribute` subclassing, `ClassWriter.getCommonSuperClass` overrides, direct constant-pool access, `Opcodes.V1_6`/version constants used when emitting.
G. The special case files: check whether compiler/asmbytecodeoptimizer/* classes define their OWN visitor class hierarchy (ByteCodeVisitor etc.) that merely *reads* classfiles via ASM, vs deeply extending ASM types.
H. Where the asm jar path appears outside java sources: grep build.xml, bin/* scripts, nbproject, and any .properties for "asm" references.

Return a structured report with concrete file:line references and a bottom-line assessment: which files need real API-shape changes vs mere recompile, and whether asm-all can be replaced by core asm alone or needs asm-util/asm-commons/asm-tree too.

## G. `asmbytecodeoptimizer` — its own hierarchy vs. deep ASM extension

43 files in the package. The design is: ASM is used **only at the two edges**.
